subtitle: A chilled Irish dry stout with roasted flavours and a creamy head, suited to drinkers who enjoy a dark, bitter pint.
quickAnswer: A Wetherspoons pint of Guinness typically costs {price}, contains {calories} kcal and is served chilled on draught with a dense, creamy white head. Prices vary by pub. Expect roasted barley, dark chocolate notes and espresso-like bitterness, with a soft mouthfeel created by the nitrogen surge.

components.name: Irish dry stout
components.note: The deep, ruby-black stout brings roasted barley and dark chocolate notes, balanced by a distinct espresso-like bitterness.

components.name: Creamy white head
components.note: The dense white head accompanies the nitrogen surge, which gives the pint its soft, velvety mouthfeel.

taste:
Guinness is a dark, roasty pint with a notably soft texture rather than a sweet chocolate flavour. Roasted barley leads the profile, with dark chocolate notes and an espresso-like bitterness providing depth. That bitterness is central to its character, so it suits someone who enjoys a pronounced roasted flavour. The smooth, velvety mouthfeel balances those stronger notes without removing them.

Served chilled on draught, it pours a deep, ruby-black colour beneath a dense, creamy white head. The nitrogen surge produces the characteristic cascade and soft texture. Its appeal is the contrast between a robust stout flavour and a gentle mouthfeel, rather than colour alone.

Vegan Chocolate Tart is another chocolate pairing to consider, drawing on the pint's dark chocolate notes and roasted bitterness.
